To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pre-harvest pearl-millet tillers and leaves can be used as animal food.
Pre-harvest pearl-millet tillers and leaves can be fed green to small ruminants.

1) green pre-harvest pearl-millet leaves and tillers can be used as a maintenance diet of ruminants; 2) conservation of leaves in silage is not advisable; 3) hay is a good conservation option; 4) small amounts of silage can be used to supplement straw diets of sheep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sustainable production systems in which the use of pre-harvest millet forages can contribute to a more efficient use of land resources.
the development of a system of crop-livestock integration in which millet is used as a forage crop for small ruminants and as a grain crop for human food.
the potential for using millet leaves for animal feed in semi-arid areas of West Africa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pre-harvest pearl-millet tillers and leaves can be used as a forage for sheep and cattle in the Sahelian region of West Africa, provided the forage is harvested at the appropriate stage, conserved as hay, or fed green to sheep and cattle.
preharvest millet leaves and tillers have a good nutritional value for ruminants.

pre-harvest pearl-millet leaves and tillers can be considered a good feed resource for small ruminants and cattle, but the nutritive value of the leaves is more variable and lower than that of the tillers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nutritive value of millet leaves is high, but the yield is low, and that the nutritive quality of millet hay was high, but the quantity of hay produced was low.
pre-harvest pearl-millet leaves and tillers have a good potential as animal feed, especially when harvested early and conserved as hay or silage.

the use of pearl millet for feeding small ruminants in semi-arid areas is a promising alternative to the use of sorghum or other crops, and that the use of pre-harvest leaves and/or tillers is a promising alternative in areas with a short rainy season.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of millet leaves as animal feed is a viable option to increase animal productivity and to reduce the need for expensive and imported feedstuffs.
the nutritive value of millet is high and can be improved by the conservation method used.
preharvest pearl millet can be a valuable source of forage for small ruminants and that the nutritional quality of the forage can be improved through silage making.
